name: Universes with an Exponential Scalar Potential
description: Spatially flat power law cosmologies with a positive exponential scalar potential, alone or with a barotropic fluid.
convention: We use $c=1$ and $\kappa^2=8\pi G$, with cosmic time $t$, conformal time $\eta$, and $a_0=a(t_0)$. The dimensionless exponent is $p$, and $t_0>0$ is the reference time.
history: Larry Abbott and Mark B. Wise used the microwave background to constrain power law inflation in 1984 [abbott_wise1984]. They studied expansion $a(t)\propto t^p$, where $t$ is cosmic time and $p>1$, and calculated the gravitational waves generated during that expansion [abbott_wise1984]. Those waves produce large scale temperature anisotropies, linking the rate of expansion to microwave temperature fluctuations [abbott_wise1984]. Francesco Lucchin and Sabino Matarrese obtained exact power law inflation from a scalar field with an exponential potential in 1985 [lucchin_matarrese1985].¶For a canonically normalized homogeneous scalar $\phi$, the potential is $V(\phi)=V_0e^{-\lambda\kappa\phi}$, with $V_0>0$, $\lambda>0$, and $\kappa^2=8\pi G$ [copeland_liddle_wands1998]. In units $c=1$, the exact scalar dominated solution has $p=2/\lambda^2$ and $\phi=2\ln(t/t_0)/(\lambda\kappa)$, for a reference time $t_0$ [heard_wands2002]. The potential amplitude fixes $t_0$ once we set $\phi(t_0)=0$. The kinetic and potential energy densities both decrease as $t^{-2}$, retaining a constant ratio [heard_wands2002]. Positive potential requires $0<\lambda^2<6$, and the expansion accelerates for $\lambda^2<2$ [heard_wands2002].¶Jonathan Halliwell established attraction toward power law inflation in 1987 [halliwell1987]. Adrian Benedict Burd and John David Barrow investigated stability in isotropic and anisotropic models in 1988 [burd_barrow1988]. Within the expanding spatially flat scalar only model, the exact power law solution attracts homogeneous scalar perturbations throughout $0<\lambda^2<6$ [heard_wands2002]. With an additional barotropic fluid, its stability requires $\lambda^2<3\gamma$ for $0<\gamma<2$, where $\gamma$ sets the fluid equation of state $p_\gamma=(\gamma-1)\rho_\gamma$ [copeland_liddle_wands1998].¶Christof Wetterich obtained another scaling behaviour in 1988 while investigating dilatation symmetry [wetterich1988]. For a scalar coupled to matter only through gravity, he found solutions whose scalar density remains a fixed fraction of the total energy density [wetterich1988]. In canonical normalization this fraction is $\Omega_\phi=\rho_\phi/(\rho_\phi+\rho_\gamma)=3\gamma/\lambda^2$, with $0<\gamma<2$ and $\lambda^2>3\gamma$ [copeland_liddle_wands1998]. The scale factor evolves as $a(t)\propto t^{2/(3\gamma)}$, so radiation gives $t^{1/2}$ and dust gives $t^{2/3}$ [wetterich1988]. Both the scalar density and the fluid density decrease as $t^{-2}$ [wetterich1988].¶Edmund J. Copeland, Andrew R. Liddle, and David Wands mapped these branches in a phase plane analysis in 1998 [copeland_liddle_wands1998]. They established that the fluid scaling solution is the late time attractor wherever it exists in expanding spatially flat models with $0<\gamma<2$ [copeland_liddle_wands1998]. Radiation has $\gamma=4/3$ and $\Omega_\phi=4/\lambda^2$, while dust has $\gamma=1$ and $\Omega_\phi=3/\lambda^2$ [copeland_liddle_wands1998]. The fluid scaling solution accelerates when $\gamma<2/3$, with the potential slope still constrained by $\lambda^2>3\gamma$ [heard_wands2002]. At $\lambda^2=3\gamma$, its fluid density vanishes and the two branches meet [copeland_liddle_wands1998].¶We define conformal time by $d\eta=dt/a(t)$ [abbott_wise1984]. When the exact power law holds for $0<t<\infty$, a future event horizon exists for $p>1$, since $\int_t^\infty dt'/a(t')$ is finite. The past integral $\int_0^t dt'/a(t')$ is finite for $1/3<p<1$, giving a particle horizon. Choosing the finite conformal endpoint as zero, we have $-\infty<\eta<0$ for $p>1$ and $0<\eta<\infty$ for $1/3<p<1$. At $p=1$, $\eta=(t_0/a_0)\ln(t/t_0)$ spans the entire real line, with $a_0=a(t_0)$. Both horizon integrals diverge in this coasting case.

related.text: The spatially flat Friedmann universe with $a(t)\propto t^p$, supported by an exponential scalar potential alone or together with a barotropic fluid.
Conformal time brings the flat spatial geometry to $ds^2=a^2(-d\eta^2+dx^2+dy^2+dz^2)$, with a conformal time interval fixed by the exponent $p$.

coordinates.name: Cosmic Cartesian

parameters.description: Expansion exponent, $p>1/3$. The scalar only branch has $p=2/\lambda^2$; the fluid scaling branch has $p=2/(3\gamma)$ and $\lambda^2>3\gamma$ with $0<\gamma<2$. The parameter $\gamma$ sets $p_\gamma=(\gamma-1)\rho_\gamma$, and the scalar fraction is $\Omega_\phi=3\gamma/\lambda^2$ on the fluid scaling branch.
Positive reference time, with dimensions of length in units $c=1$.

Dimensionless scale factor. The scalar is $\phi=2\ln(t/t_0)/(\lambda\kappa)$, with $V_0t_0^2=2(3p-1)/(\kappa^2\lambda^2)$. The parameter $\lambda$ is the dimensionless slope in $V(\phi)=V_0e^{-\lambda\kappa\phi}$.

coordinates.convention: We use comoving Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$, each with dimensions of length.

coordinates.name: Cosmic Spherical

parameters.description: Expansion exponent, $p>1/3$. The scalar only branch has $p=2/\lambda^2$; the fluid scaling branch has $p=2/(3\gamma)$ and $\lambda^2>3\gamma$ with $0<\gamma<2$. The parameter $\gamma$ sets $p_\gamma=(\gamma-1)\rho_\gamma$, and the scalar fraction is $\Omega_\phi=3\gamma/\lambda^2$ on the fluid scaling branch.
Positive reference time, with dimensions of length in units $c=1$.

Dimensionless scale factor. The scalar is $\phi=2\ln(t/t_0)/(\lambda\kappa)$, with $V_0t_0^2=2(3p-1)/(\kappa^2\lambda^2)$. The parameter $\lambda$ is the dimensionless slope in $V(\phi)=V_0e^{-\lambda\kappa\phi}$.

coordinates.convention: We use the comoving radius $r$ with dimensions of length and the dimensionless angles $(\theta,\phi)$.

coordinates.name: Conformal Time

parameters.description: Expansion exponent, $p>1/3$ and $p\ne1$. The scalar only branch has $p=2/\lambda^2$; the fluid scaling branch has $p=2/(3\gamma)$ and $\lambda^2>3\gamma$ with $0<\gamma<2$. The parameter $\gamma$ sets $p_\gamma=(\gamma-1)\rho_\gamma$, and the scalar fraction is $\Omega_\phi=3\gamma/\lambda^2$ on the fluid scaling branch.
Positive reference time, with dimensions of length in units $c=1$.

Dimensionless scale factor. The scalar is $\phi=2\ln(t/t_0)/(\lambda\kappa)$, with $V_0t_0^2=2(3p-1)/(\kappa^2\lambda^2)$. The parameter $\lambda$ is the dimensionless slope in $V(\phi)=V_0e^{-\lambda\kappa\phi}$.

coordinates.convention: We set $\eta=t_0(t/t_0)^{1-p}/[a_0(1-p)]$, with comoving Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ of length.

coordinates.name: Coasting Conformal Time

parameters.description: Positive reference time, with dimensions of length in units $c=1$.

Dimensionless scale factor. The scalar is $\phi=2\ln(t/t_0)/(\lambda\kappa)$, with $V_0t_0^2=4/(\kappa^2\lambda^2)$ at $p=1$. The parameter $\lambda$ is the dimensionless slope in $V(\phi)=V_0e^{-\lambda\kappa\phi}$.

coordinates.convention: We set $p=1$ and $\eta=(t_0/a_0)\ln(t/t_0)$, with comoving Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ of length.
